  "summary": "Clamps negative and NaN timeout values to zero in the mining interface methods WaitTipChanged and WaitAndCreateNewBlock (waitNext). It removes an Assume assertion in WaitTipChanged that aborts debug builds when a negative timeout is received, and adds functional tests for both methods.",
  "problem": "External IPC callers can pass negative or NaN timeout values to mining interface methods. In debug builds, these values trigger an Assume assertion failure that aborts the node, and in release builds, NaN values bypass simple comparison checks, causing unintended wait delays.",
  "evidence": [
    "Author note in PR description: \"On debug builds, a negative or NaN timeout fails this check and aborts the node. I reproduced this with a timeout of -1.0.\"",
    "Author note in PR description: \"Negative values are clamped to zero, but NaN is not, because every comparison with NaN is false. It ends up as the deadline passed to wait_until.\"",
    "Author note in PR description: \"I'm not aware of any client that sends these values (sv2-tp, for example, requires an interval of at least one second), so this is hardening against bad input from ipc clients.\""

result.summary: Clamps negative and NaN timeout values to zero in the mining interface methods WaitTipChanged and WaitAndCreateNewBlock (waitNext). It removes an Assume assertion in WaitTipChanged that aborts debug builds when a negative timeout is received, and adds functional tests for both methods.
result.problem: External IPC callers can pass negative or NaN timeout values to mining interface methods. In debug builds, these values trigger an Assume assertion failure that aborts the node, and in release builds, NaN values bypass simple comparison checks, causing unintended wait delays.
evidence: Author note in PR description: "On debug builds, a negative or NaN timeout fails this check and aborts the node. I reproduced this with a timeout of -1.0."
Author note in PR description: "Negative values are clamped to zero, but NaN is not, because every comparison with NaN is false. It ends up as the deadline passed to wait_until."

Author note in PR description: "I'm not aware of any client that sends these values (sv2-tp, for example, requires an interval of at least one second), so this is hardening against bad input from ipc clients."
result.card: Clamps negative and NaN timeout parameters to zero in mining interface methods WaitTipChanged and WaitAndCreateNewBlock, removing an assertion that aborts debug builds. An external IPC client passing negative or NaN values triggers an Assume crash on debug builds and bypasses comparison checks in release builds to cause wait delays. The author reproduced the debug crash with a timeout of -1.0, though notes no known IPC client currently sends negative or NaN timeouts.
